name: God Bullies
label: AmRep
lede: A Kalamazoo basement band with a preacher's name and a frontman who worked the stage like a revival tent, God Bullies turned four records for AmRep into the Michigan answer to the Twin Cities noise scene.

eras.title: A basement in Kalamazoo
eras.text: Mike Corso started the band in his basement after reconnecting with Mike Hard, who had been singing in a Kalamazoo band called Debauched. Kalamazoo was big enough to make trouble in and small enough that everybody knew everybody.

years.h: God Bullies form in Mike Corso's basement
years.p: [[Mike Hard|e61fa499-27e7-423e-9835-fe1d374ad796]] on vocals, Mike Corso on bass and Adam Berg on drums start the band in Kalamazoo, Michigan. Corso says Christian groups picketed over the name.
years.xp: According to Corso's own account, the band grew out of his basement after he reconnected with Hard. He says local church groups felt threatened by the name and showed up to picket, and that when a critic called the band "incredibly horrid" they put the line on their promo material.

years.h: First single: "All I Want Is My Mamma"
years.p: The band's debut 7" comes out on Mad Queen Records, in 1988.

years.h: A live set at Cabaret Metro, Chicago, gets pressed on a record
years.p: Four tracks from the April 20, 1988 Metro show become side two of Plastic Eye Miracle, paired with five studio songs.

eras.title: Joining the AmRep zoo
eras.text: Tom Hazelmyer's Amphetamine Reptile Records was collecting the loudest oddballs in the country, and God Bullies fit. They made three records in three years, each nastier and more sample-happy than the last, recorded at Death Jam in Detroit.

years.h: Plastic Eye Miracle: studio and live on one EP
years.p: Issued by Mad Queen Records in 1989, reissued by AmRep in 1990, with cover art by Hazelmyer. Guitarist David B. Livingstone produced and engineered it.

years.cap: Mama Womb Womb, God Bullies' first AmRep LP (1989).
years.src: Wikipedia: Mama Womb Womb · Trouser Press
years.h: Mama Womb Womb: the first full LP
years.p: Eleven songs in about 40 minutes, with a Georg Büchner text set to music on "Red Blood". Livingstone plays guitar and keys and engineers and mixes it himself.
years.xp: The lineup on the record is Mike Hard, David B. Livingstone, Mike Corso and Adam Berg, with Sue Moulds on backing vocals. It is the record Trouser Press points to for Livingstone's harsher, colder guitar tone, before he got grungier on the follow-up.

years.h: "Join Satan's Army" comes out as a double 7"
years.p: God Bullies fill two 7-inch records for AmRep, with the sermon-and-gospel-sample noise their live shows were built on.

years.h: Dog Show: the grungier, louder third LP
years.p: Recorded at Death Jam Studios in Detroit, 11 songs in about 35 minutes. Peter Houpt plays slide guitar on "Abigail" and Michael Cergizan plays guitar on "I Am Invisible".

eras.title: War on everybody
eras.text: Adam Berg and Mike Corso stepped back and the lineup started to turn over. The band kept releasing records anyway, on AmRep, then on a run of other punk labels, ending with a 1994 record for Jello Biafra's Alternative Tentacles.

years.cap: War on Everybody, God Bullies' last AmRep LP (1991).
years.src: Wikipedia: War on Everybody · Trouser Press
years.h: War on Everybody with a new rhythm section
years.p: Tony Oliveri of [[Cows|d4b064a0-5567-4930-a359-16fadfa7941b]] plays drums and Eric Polcyn plays bass, with Berg and Corso only guesting on the short "Senojmot". Recorded through summer and fall 1991 at Death Jam in Detroit.
years.xp: Hard, Livingstone, Oliveri and Polcyn are the core of the record. Bruce White sings on the opening track. At 12 songs and about 38 minutes, it is the last God Bullies LP AmRep released.

years.src: God Bullies Bandcamp · Mike Corso interview
years.p: Corso, who says he was briefly kicked out after the first three LPs, is back on bass. Hard says [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] suggested a God Bullies record to draw attention to [[Thrall|94d6bbba-8ec4-4834-ab9b-0f4c49c73315]], his new project.
years.xp: Hard told the Kill the King Bandcamp page that Biafra's idea was to make a God Bullies album that would point people toward Thrall, the Detroit band Hard was starting at the time. He reunited the original members to make it.

years.h: "Millennium" 7" on Radial Records closes the first run
years.p: The single is the last release before the band goes quiet. Hard also turns up on screen alongside Ron Asheton in the 1995 film Mosquito.

eras.title: The AmRep 25th reunion
eras.text: Amphetamine Reptile turned 25 and got its bands back on stage. God Bullies were one of the bands people talked about afterwards.

years.h: God Bullies reunite for AmRep's 25th anniversary
years.p: [[Mike Hard|e61fa499-27e7-423e-9835-fe1d374ad796]], David B. Livingstone, Mike Corso, Adam Berg and guitarist Johnnie Johnson play the label's anniversary show and a "War On Peace" tour.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, sets ran 25 to 30 songs a night. Yourfleshmag wrote that God Bullies were easily one of the three bands generating the most discussion at the anniversary event.

eras.title: Two friends gone, one record made
eras.text: Hard, Livingstone and Johnnie Johnson were working together in a new band when both men died. The surviving members finished the God Bullies album they had started.

years.p: The guitarist who engineered and mixed the AmRep-era records dies in February 2023, while working with Hard and Johnnie Johnson III on Pig Harvest, a project co-founded in November 2021. No cause is given in the sources.

q: We wanted to honor them both.
years.src: Echoes and Dust · Louder Than War · Wikipedia
years.h: Doing it for both of them
years.p: Mike Hard, Kodrik, O'Harris and Carinci reform God Bullies to finish the record with Livingstone's co-writing on it.
years.xp: Hard says Johnnie Johnson started the reunion by asking founding members to play a 25th anniversary show for Thrall. After Johnson's sudden death, the surviving members decided to complete the album for both him and Livingstone. Hard says the new lineup is largely Thrall, the Detroit band he has played with for 32 years.

years.src: Wikipedia · No Echo · Louder Than War · Echoes and Dust
years.h: As Above So Below, first LP in 30 years
years.p: Recorded at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio in Chicago with producer Sanford Parker, out October 4, 2024 on Reptilian Records. The vinyl run was 750 copies.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the sessions were in April 2024, shortly before [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s death. Hard and Kodrik say Parker pushed for a live sound with few overdubs, and the band toured the Midwest from October.
